title: routine
description: Reusable steps with declared inputs, outputs, and internals.

description.description: What the run does, and when to refer to it

anyOf.description: Qualified snake_case noun phrase of at least two words: a lowercase letter, then lowercase letters and digits, with each further word after a single underscore (`analysis_target`, never bare `target`).

id.description: Parameter name within the routine body.

description.description: What the parameter is for, in the routine's own vocabulary.

kind.description: Marks a technique-reference parameter, requiring a literal technique reference at each use or a declared default. A body technique step binding this parameter declares its own `id`, since a derived one would name the parameter.

default.description: Value for an unbound argument; without a default, a value parameter uses the host variable of the same name.

items.description: Routine parameter with an optional technique-reference kind and default.

inputs.description: Parameters for every value the body reads without producing itself.

id.description: Output name within the routine body, bound to a session variable at each use.

type.description: Type of the output and its bound session variable.

values.description: Complete set of allowed values for a string output.

optional.description: Declare `true` to allow this output to remain unbound; omission requires an output binding.

items.description: Produced value with its type, allowed values, and binding requirement.

outputs.description: Produced values, each declared with the type its bound session variable takes.

id.description: Name local to the routine body at each use, outside the workflow variable set.

description.description: What the value is, and which steps pass it.

items.description: Named value shared by steps within one use of a routine.

internals.description: Names for values shared between the routine's steps, local to each use.

id.description: Step identifier, unique within its step list (the top-level steps, or one loop body). A duplicate excludes its activity from the load; in a routine file, it excludes each activity that refers to that routine. Defaults to the last `::` segment of the technique reference; the one step kind whose id may be omitted.

additionalProperties.description: Variable name, literal value, or template expression for an input.

inputs.description: Input identifiers mapped to a source: the name of a session variable to read under that input, a literal, or a `{template}` expression. Declared only for inputs whose source differs from the same-name variable or the declared default.

additionalProperties.description: Workflow variable name for the output.

outputs.description: Output identifiers mapped to the workflow variable each value is written to. Declared only where that name differs from the output identifier.

anyOf.description: Technique reference with input and output bindings.

technique.description: Technique reference, or an object with `name` and optional `inputs` and `outputs` bindings.

action.description: Action for the executing agent to perform; a `set` value reaches the session when the agent reports it.

target.description: Variable name or other target of the action.

value.description: Value assigned or supplied by the action.

description.description: Human-readable description of what this action does

condition.description: Condition that must be true for this action to execute

items.description: Action with an optional target, value, message, and condition.

actions.description: Actions associated with the technique step.

when.description: Entry gate: the step runs only when this expression holds. On a checkpoint step, `condition`, not `when`, makes the checkpoint dismissible.

required.description: Declare `false` for an optional step; omission means the step is required, and `true` is rejected.

condition.description: Structured entry condition. Prefer `when` for a step gate. On a checkpoint step, `condition` is the only gate that makes the checkpoint dismissible: when it is false, the checkpoint may be dismissed as not met, selecting no option and no exit.

anyOf.description: Step that invokes a technique with optional actions and entry conditions.

id.description: Step identifier, unique within its step list (the top-level steps, or one loop body). A duplicate excludes its activity from the load; in a routine file, it excludes each activity that refers to that routine.

actions.description: Control actions; may be empty for marker steps.

anyOf.description: Control step with optional actions and entry conditions.

id.description: Checkpoint identifier, unique within its step list (the top-level steps, or one loop body). A duplicate excludes its activity from the load; in a routine file, it excludes each activity that refers to that routine. With the activity identifier it forms the key a recorded response replays under on resume.

additionalProperties.description: Value assigned to the named variable.

setVariable.description: Variable assignments applied when this option is selected. Each value is checked against the variable's declared type and value set, and a mismatch is stored as written with a warning; a `{name}` template value passes through unchecked.

exit.description: Exit of the owning activity this option selects: a name from its `exits`, never an activity identifier. An option naming an exit its activity does not declare fails the workflow load. Omitted for an ad hoc checkpoint, which has no declared exits.

recordReply.description: Variable that stores the text the user types with this option: a path, a correction, the change a revision asks for. `respond_checkpoint` refuses this option without a `reply`, and refuses a `reply` with any option that does not declare one. A soft checkpoint's `defaultOption` records none, which the load enforces.

effect.description: Variable assignments, the typed reply's variable, and the activity exit associated with the choice.

items.description: Checkpoint choice and its associated effects.

defaultOption.description: Identifier of one of this checkpoint's options, taken when no person answers. Declared together with `autoAdvanceMs`: the pair makes the checkpoint soft, and a hard checkpoint declares neither. One without the other, or a default naming none of the options, excludes the activity from the load; in a routine file, it excludes each activity that refers to that routine.

autoAdvanceMs.description: Positive waiting interval in milliseconds before `defaultOption` may be selected automatically; declared together with `defaultOption`.

anyOf.description: User decision at a defined position in the activity steps.

id.description: Step identifier, unique within its step list (the top-level steps, or one loop body). A duplicate excludes its activity from the load; in a routine file, it excludes each activity that refers to that routine.

loopType.description: Iteration over a collection (`forEach`), with a pre-test (`while`), or with a post-test (`doWhile`).

continueWhile.description: Continuation condition required for `while` and `doWhile` loops and absent for `forEach` loops.

variable.description: Current-item variable bound each iteration of a `forEach` loop: required there, and absent for `while` and `doWhile` loops.

over.description: Collection a `forEach` loop iterates: a variable name or a dotted path into one. Required on a `forEach` loop, and absent for `while` and `doWhile` loops.

breakCondition.description: Condition that ends a `forEach` loop before the next item; absent for `while` and `doWhile` loops.

steps.description: The loop body, a nested ordered list of steps.

anyOf.description: Loop over a collection or until a continuation test fails, entered when its `when` expression holds.

id.description: Step identifier, unique within its step list (the top-level steps, or one loop body). A duplicate excludes its activity from the load; in a routine file, it excludes each activity that refers to that routine. It is also the prefix every identifier in the routine body carries once spliced in.

routine.description: Routine reference in `[namespace::]name` form, with no segment empty. The namespace is a directory name, or the path from the corpus root reaching it. A qualified name resolves in that namespace only; a bare name resolves against the referring activity's source workflow, then `meta`. The last segment is the routine and every segment before it is the namespace, since a routine name has no group grammar.

additionalProperties.description: Literal argument or braced host-variable reference.

with.description: Routine input identifiers mapped to arguments: a braced value (`{host_variable}`) references a host variable, and any other value is a literal. An input left unbound takes its declared default, then the host variable of the same name; a `kind: technique` input left unbound with no default, or an argument naming no declared input, excludes the referring activity from the load. A `kind: technique` input takes a literal technique reference, a string holding no `{`, since the substitution happens when the definitions load and a braced value has no value then; any other argument to it excludes the referring activity from the load.

additionalProperties.description: Session variable name for the routine output.

outputs.description: Routine output identifiers mapped to session variable names. An output left unbound produces no write; only an output declared `optional: true` may be left unbound. Any other unbound output, or a binding naming no declared output, excludes the referring activity from the load.

anyOf.description: Routine invocation with argument and output bindings, entered when its `when` expression holds.

items.description: Step selected by `kind`; its guidance lives in the bound technique.

routine.description: Reusable steps with declared inputs, outputs, and internals.

whenExpression.description: Inline boolean expression in the `when` dialect, evaluated against the current session variables. Grammar: `orExpr := andExpr ('||' andExpr)*`; `andExpr := unary ('&&' unary)*`; `unary := '!' unary | primary`; `primary := IDENT | comparison | 'true' | 'false' | '(' orExpr ')'`; `comparison := IDENT ('==' | '!=' | '>' | '<' | '>=' | '<=') literal`. Precedence, tightest first: `()`, comparisons, `!`, `&&`, `||`; so `!a == b` reads as `!(a == b)`, and a negated left side of a comparison is not expressible. Mixing `&&` and `||` at the same nesting depth requires parentheses, so grouping is always explicit: `(a && b) || c`, never `a && b || c`. An IDENT is a variable name or a dotted path into one (`execution_plan.status`): a letter or underscore, then letters, digits, underscores and dots. A literal is `true`, `false`, `null`, a single- or double-quoted string (a backslash escapes the next character), an integer with an optional leading `-`, or a bare word, which is a string (`analysis_type == completion`). Decimals are not literals. A bare IDENT holds when its value is truthy. A variable that is absent is undefined: it is falsy, `==` matches nothing (not even `null` or `false`), and `!=` matches every literal. `==` and `!=` compare strictly, without type coercion. `>`, `<`, `>=` and `<=` compare numbers and strings that read as a finite number, as a structured condition does, and are false when either side is anything else, a boolean, null, an absent variable and a blank string included. An expression that does not parse evaluates to false. Examples: `has_saved_state == true`, `remediation_round > 0`, `!is_review_mode`, `a == true && b != false`, `(a && b) || c`, `is_review_mode != true && (problem_complexity == "moderate" || problem_complexity == "complex")`.

type.description: Identifies a variable comparison or presence test.

variable.description: Variable name or dot-separated path to the value to test; a path through a missing or non-object segment reads as absent.

operator.description: Comparison or presence test applied to a variable. `==` and `!=` compare strictly, without type coercion. `>`, `<`, `>=` and `<=` compare numbers and strings that read as a finite number, and are false when either side is anything else, a boolean, null, an absent value and a blank string included. `exists` holds when the value is present and not null; `notExists` holds when it is absent or null.

value.description: Comparison value; unnecessary for `exists` and `notExists` tests.

anyOf.description: Comparison of a variable with a value, or a test of its presence.

conditions.description: At least two conditions that must all be true.

anyOf.description: Condition requiring every member to be true.

conditions.description: At least two conditions, one or more of which must be true.

anyOf.description: Condition requiring at least one member to be true.
Condition requiring its member to be false.

condition.description: Variable test or combination of conditions using `and`, `or`, or `not`.

techniqueReference.description: Technique reference: `[namespace::]technique[::nested…]`, segments separated by `::`, none of them empty. When its leading segments spell a namespace the corpus holds and at least one segment follows them, the rest of the path resolves in that namespace and nowhere else. A namespace is spelled by its directory name, by the path from the corpus root that reaches it, or by as much of the end of that path as reaches it alone (`gitnexus` and `support::gitnexus` name the same one); the longest leading run that spells a namespace wins. Otherwise every segment is a path under the referring workflow's `techniques/`, the first naming a group and the last the technique, resolved in the referring workflow and then in `meta`; a borrowed activity's referring workflow is the one it is borrowed from. On a step, a one-segment reference resolves first as `<activity-id>::<name>`, in the group named after the activity, and as written where that group holds no such technique. A reference that reads both ways is refused, naming both files. The spelling `namespace/technique` names a namespace, whether or not the corpus holds one; a second slash, or a slash after a `::`, is malformed. Where no nested technique matches, the last segment names a rule on the technique before it, and a group name `{group}` stands for every rule named `{group}-*`.
